purpose: Challenge the sole Campaign062 quarterly disclosure-attention mechanism against all nearest terminal families and freeze one exact definition before any Campaign062 source value is read.

selected_mechanism.name: quarterly_announcement_peer_crowding_sparsity
selected_mechanism.economic_hypothesis: Lower same-report-period disclosure crowding reduces cross-issuer competition for investor attention and may permit slower firm-specific information diffusion over the next three sessions.
selected_mechanism.formula: For each unique instrument-report_date event, peer_count is the number of distinct instruments sharing exact report_date and exact announcement_date. On each stock-day use the latest strictly-prior-announced effective event, resolving simultaneous effective events by later report_date, and return 1/peer_count.
selected_mechanism.peer_definition: all distinct instruments in the immutable source sharing both exact report_date and exact announcement_date; include the issuer itself
selected_mechanism.point_in_time_rule: the event becomes usable on the first accepted session strictly after announcement_date

overlap_challenges.reason: Freshness changes with accepted-session age after one issuer's disclosure. Campaign062 remains constant with age and changes only when the same report-period/date peer count changes.

Timeliness is the issuer's calendar-day delay from report date to announcement date. Holding those issuer dates fixed while changing peer issuers on the same pair changes Campaign062 but leaves timeliness unchanged.

Delay consistency requires four consecutive issuer reports and measures within-issuer delay dispersion. Campaign062 needs only the latest effective event and measures cross-issuer attention competition.
Campaign062 projects no accounting value and is invariant to every quarterly value field while event identities and dates remain fixed.

Generic event intensity counts multiple notices for one issuer or decays their age. Campaign062 counts other issuers only after exact standardized report-period and announcement-date alignment, and has no same-issuer multiplicity term.
Campaign062 reads no minute OHLCV/amount, transaction price, market peer return, or cross-session price path. Holding the quarterly event table fixed makes it invariant to every minute path.

Candidate49 is a future-only causal minute close/volume/amount crossing statistic. Campaign062 uses disclosure identities only, includes Candidate49 solely in the no-return uniqueness library, and never reads its historical return.
Campaign061 compares squared minute close-return scale across two adjacent stock sessions. Campaign062 has no price, return, lagged stock session, or volatility input.

counterfactual_independence_tests: Holding one issuer's report_date and announcement_date fixed while adding or removing a different issuer with the same pair changes Campaign062 and leaves issuer freshness, timeliness, and delay consistency unchanged.
Advancing the stock-day while keeping the latest effective event unchanged changes freshness but leaves Campaign062 unchanged.
Changing quarterly accounting values while keeping event identities and dates fixed leaves Campaign062 unchanged.
Changing every minute price, range, volume, amount, market-peer, and prior-session path while keeping quarterly event identities fixed leaves Campaign062 unchanged.

decision.next_action: Freeze the exact source fingerprints, coverage-first gates, 93-factor comparison order, and single development trial before reading Campaign062 source values.
